title: The Delhi Monkey Man
sources: BBC News, 'Delhi's mysterious monkey man' (May 2001: mass panic across East Delhi, Ghaziabad, Noida; two deaths from falling/stampede; dozens treated for scratches)
The Guardian, 'Mystery monkey man terrorises Delhi' (May 18, 2001: police switchboards overwhelmed, 50,000 rupee reward offered)
Time Magazine, 'The Monkey Man of Delhi' (Medical and psychiatric evaluation concluded the phenomenon was mass sociogenic illness exacerbated by heat and power cuts)

lines.text: In two thousand and one, Delhi was gripped by a terrifying urban legend,
lines.caps: In *2001, | Delhi was *gripped | by an *urban legend,

lines.text: where people were terrified to sleep on their own rooftops.
It was a sweltering May, and everyone was whispering about the Monkey Man.
lines.caps: A sweltering *May, | whispering of the *Monkey Man.

lines.text: Witnesses described a four foot beast with glowing red eyes,
leaping between buildings in the pitch dark.
Police switchboards exploded with hundreds of frantic emergency calls,
as terrified families huddled together under streetlights.
Dozens were injured, and two people tragically died in the panic.
Yet the mysterious creature was never captured,
and police concluded the sightings were driven entirely by mass hysteria.
Was it a real attacker, an urban myth, or India's biggest mass panic?
